subject: Intermittent streaming silence reported by Sunrise Health — investigation concluded
messages:
From: Alex Morton <alex@sunrisehealth.com>
To: support@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 16:42:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming responses sometimes return empty payloads during large patient-summary runs

Hi team,

We saw another occurrence this morning where our nightly batch (30k requests) produced ~12 requests that returned an empty streaming payload — connection stayed open, then closed without tokens. This is intermittent (~0.04% of requests). Happened between 03:05–03:12 PST.

We collect request ids; attaching a small tar with request traces and the SDK snippet we use. Can you check for any platform outages or quota throttles correlated to these times?

Thanks,
Alex
Senior Platform Engineer
Sunrise Health

Attachments: sunrise_sample_logs.tar.gz, sdk-request-snippet.txt

From: support@redwood.com <support@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morton <alex@sunrisehealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 17:05:48 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming responses sometimes return empty payloads during large patient-summary runs

Hi Alex — thanks for the report and the logs. We've opened INC-20280704-2047 and assigned an engineer to reproduce. Initial questions:

- Can you share the request IDs for the five earliest occurrences you see in the tar? We want exact ids to look up traces.
- Which SDK version and language are you using?
- Do you see client-side disconnects (socket close) on your side or only empty payloads?

Connor will try to replay the requests in a staging cluster and correlate with service-side traces. We'll update within 24 hours.

— Redwood Support

From: Alex Morton <alex@sunrisehealth.com>
To: support@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Anand <priyaa@sunrisehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Jul 2028 08:13:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming responses sometimes return empty payloads during large patient-summary runs

Thanks — the five earliest request ids are: r_20280703_030512_aa12, r_20280703_030528_bb03, r_20280703_030534_cc77, r_20280703_030559_dd21, r_20280703_030603_ee45.

We're on redwood-sdk-java v1.8.2. We did not observe socket closes on the client; the stream stayed open for ~8–12s and then ended with no tokens. Attaching the same truncated logs for quick reference.

Alex

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morton <alex@sunrisehealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Jul 2028 09:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming responses sometimes return empty payloads during large patient-summary runs

Hi Alex — I replayed the five request ids in staging and ran them against the same model + sequence length distribution you provided. Repro steps: replayed payload, forced identical rate/headers, and looked up internal traces via the request ids you shared. Findings:

- No systemic error on the serving layer during the timestamps provided. Traces for r_20280703_030512_aa12 show standard token generation with one short-lived kernel preemption that increased latency but still returned tokens.
- For r_20280703_030528_bb03 and r_20280703_030534_cc77 we saw client reconnect events in the upstream proxy logs that correspond to brief TCP retransmits from a Sunrise edge node. Those client-side network retries would explain an interrupted streaming payload.
- r_20280703_030559_dd21 and r_20280703_030603_ee45 show no platform-side errors; both returned full token streams in staging reproduction.

Conclusion: we could not reproduce a platform-origin empty payload. Two of the instances correlate with network instability on the customer edge; the remainder appear unreproducible from Redwood's traces.

Next steps we took:
- Enabled additional logging for the serving gateway for the next 72 hours for any requests from Sunrise Health (sampling 1:10 to limit load).
- Added a temporary rule to capture full connection metadata for requests coming from Sunrise IP ranges.
- Notified the infra team to watch for any kernel-preemption patterns on the GPU fleet (no actionable signal so far).

Could you confirm whether your edge team observed any packet drops or proxy timeouts around 03:05–03:12 PST? If you can share packet captures that would help.

— Connor

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morton <alex@sunrisehealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Jul 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming responses sometimes return empty payloads during large patient-summary runs — closure

Hi Alex / Priya — thank you for your patience while we investigated. Summary and closure: 

Summary:
- We investigated the five reported occurrences and attempted reproductions in staging with identical inputs and SDK version.
- No platform-origin defect was identified. Two events correlate with client-side network instability at your edge (retransmits/reconnects seen in our proxy logs). The other three did not reproduce and returned full streams when replayed.

Actions taken by Redwood:
- Enabled elevated logging and a short-lived capture rule for Sunrise Health traffic for 72 hours (sampling enabled).
- Confirmed no quota throttles, no controller-level errors, and no model degradation in the time window.
- Created monitoring alert tied to an elevated empty-stream ratio for your account (threshold 0.1% sustained over 1 hour) and linked alert to your account contacts.
- Documented recommended mitigations in the shared playbook: upgrade to redwood-sdk-java v1.9.0 (contains improved reconnect semantics), add client-side retry backoff, and add a short keepalive so downstream proxies do not tear idle streams. Playbook link: https://docs.redwood.com/playbooks/streaming-troubleshooting

Recommendation: work with your edge team to review the proxy logs and packet captures during the time windows we shared. If you capture a sample that clearly shows no TCP-level disconnects and the downstream saw a FIN without tokens, reopen the ticket and we'll escalate to infra for a deeper kernel-level trace.

Closing now as "no platform evidence" — please reopen if you observe a reproducible pattern or can share additional traces. We're standing by to help.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
